bullets.title: NVDA beats and raises FY28 to +75% growth; leadership transition dominates debate
bullets.body: NVDA reported $115.8B revenue with $107.6B data center sales, guided Q4 to $130B, and raised FY28 revenue growth to 75% from 70% despite Jensen Huang's exit and new China export restrictions ($2.4B Hopper sales halted). Interim CEO Colette Kress emphasized selectivity in neocloud financing and confirmed Vera Rubin GPU ramp is fastest in history with ~$20B in first-quarter revenue. Street is split: UBS cut CY28 estimates ~15%, Piper lowered PT to $230 (from ~14x to 10x CY28E PE), while DA Davidson and Goldman noted no demand problem — NVDA now trades ~9x forward P/E with $227B buyback authorization.

bullets.title: Post-midterm positioning flush: systematic funds sold ~$116B, exposure at 10th percentile
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Prime reported $4.3T notional traded in 3 days post-midterms, the second-largest VVIX spike on record (trailing only 2018 Volmageddon), and 11M+ puts traded on Nov 5 — the largest single-day put volume ever on Cboe. Systematic strategies sold ~$116B in two weeks pushing aggregate equity exposure to the 10th percentile; hedge fund momentum exposure collapsed to 23rd percentile. DB notes global equity funds attracted $98.3B in the latest week (99.7th percentile), and SPX dealer gamma at -$7.3B means another 5% decline could trigger ~$81.8B mechanical selling.

bullets.title: Fed's Waller abandons rhetoric-only approach; signals actual Dec/Jan rate hikes needed
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller broke from the FOMC's pattern of using hawkish rhetoric as a substitute for action, explicitly advocating 25bps hikes in both December and January to break the 3% inflation psychology now embedded among firms. Analysis suggests the FOMC may need 4+ total hikes to undo 2025 risk-management cuts, with Druckenmiller reporting Treasury Secretary Warsh is deeply unhappy with 15 years of accommodative policy. The broader FOMC is more likely to harden rhetoric than deliver a 50bps December move, but the hurdle for a December+January dual-hike path is lower than for 50bps in a single meeting.

bullets.title: Housing data deteriorates sharply: permits at cycle low, pending sales at all-time low
bullets.body: October single-family building permits fell 8.9% m/m to their lowest level since 2022, while pending home sales dropped 4.7% m/m to an all-time low, pointing to existing home sales sliding toward 3.6M annualized — lowest since 2010. Mortgage rates climbed 19bps with purchase apps declining 2.3% w/w; Morgan Stanley revised 4Q residential investment tracking to -6.0% (q/q ar) from prior +1.0%. Affordability crisis requires both rate declines and time for incomes to catch up with prices.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO 7x oversubscribed at ~$1.69T market cap; AI platform valuations surging
bullets.body: Anthropic's IPO is nearly 7x oversubscribed with ~$400B institutional and $100B retail demand, pricing well above the initial $70-78 range and exceeding SpaceX's record $85.7B IPO demand. Current estimated market cap stands at $1.689T, up 387% from its November 2025 listing at $347B. OpenAI separately raised $15B at $1.25T valuation and expects $70B+ annualized revenue by end of 2026, underscoring the intensity of private AI platform capital formation.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure demand intact: AMD supply-constrained, DELL has 6,500 AI factories, ALAB content doubling
bullets.body: TomorrowX conference commentary uniformly bullish on AI buildout: AMD CEO described demand as 'substantially higher' than supply with Venice and MI455 Helios performing 'extremely' well at META, MSFT, and ORCL. DELL CEO confirmed no change to bullish view with 6,500 AI factories across a diverse non-hyperscaler customer base. ALAB noted content per accelerator is doubling every 18 months, benefiting from copper-to-optical transition; CBRS flagged >75% of 2027 data center capacity coming online outside the US.

bullets.title: SOX down 25-35% from highs; tech L/S ratio at 2016 lows — positioning argues for pain trade higher
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down 25% from mid-October highs and 35% from June all-time highs. Goldman Prime data shows tech L/S ratio at 2016 lows, hedge fund nets at rock bottom, and CTAs likely max short NDX. AI/semis shorts are largely exhausted as hedge funds cover and real money buys dips; UBS equity finance reported tech net short with shorts +10.9% WoW but top covered names include GOOG, AMZN, META. SPX support cited at 7,300 with below-that target of 7,000; rally target 7,600 on event clearing.

bullets.title: 10-year yield at 5.10%; copper -4%, industrial metals signal growth deceleration
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield ticked up 1bp to 5.10% in pre-market while copper futures fell 4% and tin dropped 8%, with cross-asset signals pointing to a deteriorating macro backdrop. Hedgeye's GDP nowcast shows US growth decelerating from 3.48% in Q4 2026 to 1.4% in Q1 2027. All major equity indices breached their 200-day moving averages with negative momentum and weak breadth, though Q4 real PCE is tracking ~2.5% annualized vs Bloomberg consensus of 2%.

bullets.title: $3.6T in equity options expire Friday; below-average expiry but watch delta-hedging volatility
bullets.body: $3.6T notional open interest expires November 20 (comprising $2.2T indices, $690B ETFs, $742B single stocks), the smallest monthly expiry since April 2026 though above historical November levels. The expiry represents 4.8% of Russell 3000 market cap, below long-term average. Fifty options chains have strikes within +/-2% of current price with significant open interest relative to daily volumes, flagging potential delta-hedging-driven single-name volatility into Friday.

bullets.title: MSFT in advanced talks to provide $500M Azure compute to ByteDance; OpenAI privately objects
bullets.body: Microsoft is in advanced talks to provide $500M of cloud computing services to ByteDance for OpenAI models on Azure, with ByteDance on track to spend over $1B/year on Microsoft AI and cloud. The deal has upset OpenAI, which has complained privately to Microsoft about insufficient prevention of Chinese companies copying its models. Separately, the US Treasury and White House OSTP are discussing requiring US companies to publicly disclose use of Chinese AI models on their websites.

bullets.title: Texas TCEQ air permit issued for SPCX 750MW data center; Dec 10 ERCOT review is key gating date
bullets.body: Texas environmental regulators approved an air permit for SpaceX's $24B data center project in Brownsville's Rio Grande Valley (35 turbines, up to 750MW). The December 10 ERCOT comprehensive audit report remains the key gating date for DC energization approvals in Texas post-midterms; analysts caution that ERCOT — not TCEQ — still controls actual DC energization. NVDA interim CEO Kress explicitly cited land, power, and shell availability as a critical priority for future financing support of data center buildout, reinforcing the powered-shell investment thesis.

bullets.title: SpaceX terrestrial wireless strategy perceived as structural negative for tower stocks
bullets.body: SpaceX's emerging terrestrial wireless ambitions are being read as a negative catalyst for cell tower REITs, with SBAC down 6.5%, CCI down 5.8%, and AMT down 4% on the news. The move adds a new competitive overhang to an already rate-pressured tower sector.

bullets.title: Japan nominal exports +21% y/y on price inflation; BoJ faces wage-inflation pressure
bullets.body: Japan's nominal exports surged 21.1% y/y in October driven by 16.9% export price inflation, but real goods exports rose only 1.6% y/y with real GDP contracting -0.1% q/q in Q3. Nominal semiconductor trade is booming as AI drives chip price inflation. Rengo is targeting a 6% wage increase for the 2027 Shunto with a 5% minimum floor, with core CPI at a record high and all Tokyo CPIs above the BoJ's 2% target — reinforcing pressure for continued BoJ tightening.

bullets.title: Japan/Korea buyback reform provides structural equity support; AI dividend growth underappreciated in Nikkei
bullets.body: Japan buyback announcements exceeded ¥25T YTD 2026 with ¥14T executed, outperforming TOPIX by 7% YTD; Korea KOSPI buyback announcements reached ~KRW90T. JPMorgan's Asia derivatives team recommends TPX call spreads and NKY KO calls for cost-efficient upside, noting AI-related dividend growth is forecast to reach 35% of Nikkei dividend points by 2028 (vs 22% now), with AI semiconductor/data-centre companies driving 54% annual dividend growth through 2028.

bullets.title: Retail earnings mixed: TJX strong on comps, Lowe's and Home Depot face margin/guidance headwinds
bullets.body: TJX beat with total Q3 comps +4% (vs 3% est), raised FY27 revenue guidance to $63.8-64.0B, and boosted buyback to ~$3.0B, benefiting from $463M in cumulative tariff refunds. Lowe's Q3 comp beat (+1.8% vs +0.1% est) was largely driven by a $0.34 tariff refund EPS contribution, with gross margin down to 33.0% from 34.2% and Q4 comps implied at 0-1%; fuel and freight cost acceleration is expected to carry into 2027. Home Depot showed +2.2% comps with market share gains but faces a softening housing backdrop.

bullets.title: NVDA neocloud financing shift signals more scrutiny on credit counterparties
bullets.body: NVDA interim CEO Colette Kress stated the company is taking a 'very strong look' at credit counterparties in neocloud financing, signaling increased discipline rather than a broad pullback. UBS notes $70B in purchase commitments for F4Q vs $38B COGS guidance, with DSO rising due to direct-build customers taking extended payment terms to remove margin stacking. No major financing cutback was signaled but the higher bar for NVDA backstopping customer sales is a new overhang on leveraged neocloud names.

bullets.title: Chip export control tightening imminent; Congressional pressure accelerating MATCH/AI Overwatch acts
bullets.body: Tighter export controls on semiconductors to China appear imminent per Piper's morning note citing Congressional pressure and pending AI Overwatch, MATCH, and Chip Security Acts. NVDA has already halted Hopper/H200 sales to China (~$2.4B in F3Q revenue). Democrats are separately investigating whether Commerce Secretary Lutnick helped Cantor Fitzgerald avoid losses linked to an Nvidia-related scandal, adding political risk to the export control trajectory.

bullets.title: Atlanta Fed GDPNow at 3.4% for Q4 but macro rotation toward defensives underway
bullets.body: Atlanta Fed GDPNow is tracking 3.4% for Q4 vs ~2% economic speed limit, with October control retail sales beating and Q4 real PCE on track for ~2.5% annualized vs Bloomberg consensus of 2%. Despite resilient near-term data, cross-asset signals (copper -4%, tin -8%, 200-day MA breaches across all major indices) point to a deteriorating outlook, with 22V and OPCO recommending rotation to staples, healthcare, REITs, and utilities. A durable Cyclicals-vs-Defensives upturn is unlikely until both inflation and growth slow.

bullets.title: Chile Central Bank flags elevated debt risks from AI-linked companies and high valuations of risky assets
bullets.body: Chile's Central Bank flagged elevated global financial risks including rising debt among AI-linked companies and high valuations of risky assets, noting domestic financing conditions have tightened and borrower repayment capacity has weakened. This is an early emerging-market regulator signal echoing the broader concern about AI capex leverage sustainability.

bullets.title: Cloudflare accelerates GAAP profitability path by ~2 years; AI agent workloads emerging as major growth vector
bullets.body: Cloudflare management reported that path to GAAP profitability has moved forward by almost two years as Workers and Workers AI scale improves unit economics, with network footprint now covering ~30% of web. AI agent workloads are emerging as a major growth vector given the platform's CPU-intensive orchestration architecture, with 'Act Four' AI monetization (content signaling, agent transactions, wallets, identity) expected to become larger than earlier phases. Leading indicators remain strong: pipeline, sales productivity, retention, and RPO are all ahead of expectations.
